beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. The shortcut is to ask Claude for a game and submit whatever runs. Assignment one asks for something stronger: an extension whose changes you can explain and whose limits you can show. Shipping Lane is our worked example.

beats.narration_text: Five terms. A starter is the existing game you extend. A collider is the boundary physics uses. A regression check tests behavior that must survive a change. A fixture is a controlled test setup, not a human playtest. A revision identifies the exact source being demonstrated.

beats.narration_text: Here is the working loop. Write the brief, make one bounded change, run the game, inspect what happened, and revise from that evidence. Walker is a set of instructions and tools for following that loop. It does not replace your judgment.

beats.narration_text: Your task starts with Walker Jumpman, not an empty project. Change the character meaningfully and add at least two jump landings beyond the original route. Move the finish. Shipping Lane goes further, but blocks, bugs and power-ups are example choices, not extra assignment requirements.

beats.narration_text: Use your own copy or a course-authorized repository, with a name beginning walker dash. Credit the starter. Import its project file in Godot rather than creating an empty project. Use your course Claude Code access; paid assets and purchased credits are not required.

beats.narration_text: Before edits, write your character concept, the new player decision, the behavior to preserve, and at least two failures with checks. Keep those first predictions. The Shipping Lane brief predicted hidden camera or label problems and a raised landing that the unchanged jump might not clear.

beats.narration_text: Ask Claude to read the README, build report and change brief, then locate drawing, collider, level data, camera, finish and tests. Require a plan before editing. beats.act: II · Change The Character, Keep The Contract
beats.narration_text: Inspect the starter drawing before choosing an art pipeline. This version routes drawing into Clawd Art. Its broad body, arms, eyes and legs make it recognizable, not merely recolored. The movement function remains separate. A new drawing does not automatically define a new physics body.

beats.narration_text: Record what must survive. This example keeps speed, jump velocity, gravity and the collision body. If a new landing is impossible, revise the geometry first. Do not remove collision checks or increase jump strength simply to turn a failed route into a passing report.

beats.act: III · Extend The Route, Not Just The Floor
beats.narration_text: Read First Steps and its session code together. Shipping Lane keeps the original route and appends new decisions beyond it. Width grows from nine hundred sixty to three thousand two hundred units, and the finish moves to thirty-one hundred twelve. These are this example’s values, not a prescribed student layout.

Backgrounds, labels, hazard art and the finish must agree with the data too. Inspect the next landing before jumping; a physically reachable platform can still be hidden from the player.

beats.narration_text: The interface needs the same repair. This version computes progress from spawn to the current finish rather than keeping the old fixed distance. beats.act: III · Extend The Route, Not Just The Floor
beats.narration_text: One real attempt stalled at horizontal position twenty-two thirty. A reward block obstructed the raised-lane approach. beats.narration_text: The example also adds blocks. This source marks a block used before changing its tile or emitting the reward, so repeated head contact cannot pay twice. if kind == "brick":

beats.heading: Block, spark, brick, shield
beats.narration_text: The block becomes used. The spark grants a shield. Powered Clawd breaks a brick, then spends the shield on enemy contact.

beats.narration_text: The original route fixture belongs to the original map. Keep its assertions and run it against that layout. Add a separate full-level route for Shipping Lane. That new route checks four landings, the finish, camera, replay, pause and retry. Green output is meaningful only when you can explain what was checked.

beats.narration_text: Ten points concern the honest Frictional log; ten concern matching accessible versions on GitHub and Canvas. Twenty are comparative after the group is reviewed. Meeting the fixed criteria can earn the other eighty, not guarantee the comparative twenty. Use Canvas for the deadline; the daily late penalty is ten percent.

beats.heading: From First Steps to the new finish
beats.narration_text: This is the actual course, driven by scripted keyboard input. The original First Steps route still works. Beyond its old finish, Clawd crosses four new gaps, reads walking bugs, climbs the raised lane and reaches the shipping flag. The camera follows the extended bounds. Completion and replay work without collecting every token. This demonstrates a route, not a human judgment about difficulty.
